title: fix(objectql): the loser of a concurrent update answers 409 again on an object with a metadata beforeUpdate hook
body:
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
https://claude.ai/code/session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt

Fixes #35142

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：凡是自开事务单元的 update（对象带元数据 `beforeUpdate` 钩子，或带阻断式 / 带条件的元数据 `afterUpdate` 钩子），「after-abort 事务单元」原先包住整个写入（含授权中间件），现在只包住引擎本体（钩子、写行、after 链）；中间件在事务开启之前运行，与无钩子对象一致。
- **为什么改**：在 SQLite（单连接）上两人同时认领同一条记录时，输家等赢家提交后才做授权读，被拒为 404（private）或 403（public_read），而不是 ADR-0142 D4 承诺的 `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`。`beforeUpdate` 钩子一支自 18.6.0 起出错（18.5.0 为 409）；阻断式 `afterUpdate` 钩子一支在 18.5.0 已是 404/403。HotCRM 的 18.6.0 升级被它挡住。
- **风险与回滚**：风险在于中间件 `next()` 之后的代码对这类 update 改为在提交之后运行，与无钩子对象一致；`beforeUpdate` 一支等于回到 18.5.0，阻断式 `afterUpdate` 一支则是新变化（18.0.0 至 18.6.0 都在事务内运行）。钩子侧写回滚（#34503 的目的）不变。回滚 = revert 本 PR 的 `engine-update.ts` 一处改动。
- **先看**：`packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts`（门入口 `ownUnit`/`inOwnUnit` 与 `executeWithMiddleware(opCtx, inOwnUnit(...))` 两处）；`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/ownership-claim-race-sqlite.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**：`cd packages/plugins/plugin-security && pnpm exec vitest run src/ownership-claim-race-sqlite.test.ts`，预期 7/7 通过；五格各 25 轮，输家全部为 `CONCURRENT_UPDATE/409`。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`UpdateFacet.update` no longer re-enters itself inside `inAfterAbortUnit` at the door. It decides at the door whether the write needs its own unit (`opensAfterAbortUnit`, unchanged), and wraps only the executor it hands to `executeWithMiddleware` in that unit. So the middleware chain (the authorization gate's caller-scoped pre-image read among it) runs before `BEGIN`, the way it does for an update that opens no unit, and everything the unit exists for (the `before*` hooks and their `ctx.api` side writes, the row write, the `after*` chain) still runs inside it and rolls back together.

The change applies to any update that opens its own unit, which is `opensAfterAbortUnit`'s whole answer, and that predicate has two arms:

- **`sideWriting`: a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook.** `a8e09bbc31` (#34503) added this term (traced in the card's trace comment), new in 18.6.0. Race answer: `409` in 18.5.0, `404` / `403` in 18.6.0, `409` again here.
- **`aborting`: a blocking (`onError` `abort`, the default) or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook (#22782).** Its door-level unit already shipped in `@objectstack/objectql@18.5.0`: `engine-update.ts:151-153` at tag `@objectstack/objectql@18.5.0` (`b914e7247f`) reads `if (this.opensAfterAbortUnit('afterUpdate', object, options?.context)) { return this.inAfterAbortUnit(() => this.update(object, data, options)); }`, and that tag's `opensAfterAbortUnit` has the `aborting` term and no `sideWriting` term. Race answer: `404` / `403` already in 18.5.0 and in 18.6.0 (the new fifth cell reads `RECORD_NOT_FOUND/404` x25 on main's `engine-update.ts`), `409` here for the first time.

With the unit around the whole door, the SQLite driver's single connection made the loser's whole write, gate included, wait for the winner's commit. The gate then read a row owned by the winner and refused: 404 under `private`, 403 under `public_read`. The conditional write whose 0-row answer is `ConcurrentUpdateError` was never reached.

Insert and delete keep their door-level unit. Measured with the same rig, 20 rounds per cell, `private` and `public_read`, with and without a metadata `before*` hook on the verb:

- Concurrent insert of one id: the loser answers `DUPLICATE_RECORD/409` in all four cells. No race-shaped defect, so no change.
- Concurrent delete of one row: with no hook the loser's `delete` resolves `false`; with a hook it answers `RECORD_NOT_FOUND/404`. Both say the row is gone, which it is. D4 governs updates, and the 404 is not a lie about a readable row. So it stays out of this PR's scope (see Acceptance notes).

What a middleware does after `next()` on an update that opens its own unit now runs after the commit, as it does on every update that opens no unit. For the `beforeUpdate` arm that is how 18.5.0 behaved. For the `afterUpdate` arm it is a change, not a return: in every release from 18.0.0 (the first `@objectstack/objectql` tag whose source calls `opensAfterAbortUnit`; 17.7.0 has 0 hits) through 18.6.0, that code ran inside the row's unit on an object with a blocking or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook. The post-`next()` code that runs on an update in this tree:

- plugin-security authz: the `postHookWriteImageCheck` honoured-flag assertion (it fails closed if the engine never ran the seam; the engine always runs it inside the executor), then field-level masking of the result (no write).
- plugin-security start hooks: the platform-admin bootstrap replay (`shouldReplayBootstrapFor`) and the `sys_member` org-admin grant reconcile (writes, `sys_member` only).
- organizations, plugin-auth, runtime app-plugin, plugin-sharing: post-`next()` branches that act on insert/create only.

On a `sys_member` update that opens its own unit, the org-admin grant reconcile is no longer in the same unit as the row. With a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook that matches 18.5.0; with a blocking or conditioned metadata `afterUpdate` hook it is new. Either way it matches every unhooked object.

## Tests

New pin `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/ownership-claim-race-sqlite.test.ts`: the real `ObjectQL`, `SqlDriver` on better-sqlite3 `:memory:`, `SecurityPlugin` and `SharingService`. It has five cells, 25 rounds each: `private`/`public_read`, each with and without a metadata `beforeUpdate` hook, plus `private` on an object whose only metadata hook is a blocking `afterUpdate` (`onError: 'abort'`), which holds the predicate's other arm. Every round asserts that exactly one claim fulfils, that the loser's `{code}/{status}` is `CONCURRENT_UPDATE/409`, and that the stored owner is the winner. Two non-regression cases run on the hooked `private` object: a deleted row answers `RECORD_NOT_FOUND/404`, and a row owned by someone else answers as not found, never as forbidden (no existence leak).

## Acceptance notes

- Concurrent delete answers the loser differently by unit shape: `false` with no metadata `beforeDelete` hook, `RECORD_NOT_FOUND/404` with one. No declared contract picks between them, and neither misreports a readable row. Noted, not filed.
- Insert and delete keep their door-level unit, so their middleware's post-`next()` work stays inside it while update's does not. Whether they should move the same way is carried by #35167.
- overlap-check at `d9fe9175e7`: origin/main and #34978 (shares `engine-update.ts`) both merge cleanly.

## Verification

On head `d9fe9175e7` (merge base `99a0e4fbf`; overlap-check against origin/main and #34978: merges cleanly, so main is not merged in again), `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 70 families, and all 70 exit 0 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` found their dists this time and measured). `check:query-options-erasure` and `check:type-check-debt` each outran a 240 s per-gate runner timeout and exited 0 when rerun alone. `--ran` reconciliation with exit codes: 70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. Between `99c200dbb1` and `d9fe9175e7` only the changeset text moved, so the race-test runs above (7/7 at `99c200dbb1`) read the same test and engine bytes. `test:repo` and the plugin-security suite outside the new file are left to CI (Test Core). The objectql public surface is byte-unchanged.
